_comment: What the library is allowed to sound like. Read by src/debug/Audition.ts.
`rules` are absolute and need no history. `models` is recorded history and
catches drift — a change to a shared primitive that moves six models nobody
was thinking about. That is the case for having a row per model: `impact`
has nine consumers, `clock` seven, `modal` five, and a one-line change to
any of them is exactly the change where nobody re-listens to everything.
Rows are produced by running the audition in a browser (?debug -> sound
stage -> audition the library) and pasting what it prints. Re-capture after
a change you meant; a drift you did not mean is what this is for.
## What is deliberately NOT checked
`bands` is recorded and printed and never asserted on. Eight numbers per
model is 120 tripwires that largely restate the centroid, and every honest
tuning change trips several of them. They are kept because reading them is
what caught the friction model coming out spectrally flat — a diagnostic,
not a gate.
Loudness is not compared across the library either. The first version
required every model to sit within 3 units of every other, and the real
spread is 23: a wind bed renders at -47 and an engine at -27. That is
correct — a zone spec sets gain, refDistance and maxDistance, so the mixing
happens at placement and intrinsic loudness at defaults is not the thing
being mixed. The spread is reported for interest and asserted on never.
Per-model loudness drift is the check that survived, and it is the one that
was always doing the work.
Peak over average, in dB, and it means opposite things for the two
kinds of source — which is why there are two bands rather than one.
A continuous texture with a very high crest is bubble wrap: audible
individual grains. An impulsive source with a *low* one has lost its
transient and turned into a wash. Bounds are drawn wide around the
first captured run rather than derived; the drift check below is the
sharp instrument, and these only catch a model that has fallen over.
